ai.description: This small skink reaches 5 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a dark lateral band and pale dorsolateral stripes. Key features include a transparent palpebral disc and smooth scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kaestlea travancorica* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous pale dorsolateral stripe bordered by a dark band, which is absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: Kaestlea travancorica inhabits the leaf litter of moist evergreen and shola forests in the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: Kaestlea travancorica is a diurnal lizard that actively hunts for small invertebrates among leaf litter, relying on its cryptic coloration to blend into the forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kaestlea travancorica* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kaestlea travancorica* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,000 meters.
